# NFSU.cc — Reverse Engineering, Static Recompilation (x86 to WebAssembly) & Live Demo

> Open-source field guide to binary reverse engineering, ahead-of-time x86-to-C static recompilation, DirectX 9-to-WebGPU translation, and browser WebAssembly performance — proven live by running Need for Speed Underground (2003, PC `Speed.exe`) in a browser tab at https://nfsu.cc/ with no emulator.

Primary production evidence: `Speed.exe` (3.18 MB, md5 `b6b9232c55376b3c38c56aac1f8a121d`, `13,766` x86 functions lifted to C and compiled to WebAssembly), `15,035` LOC C host layer (Win32, DirectX 9 -> WebGPU/WebGL 2 with native BC1/2/3 textures, DirectInput, DirectSound -> Web Audio), `49` verified subsystem monographs (`2,858` unique hex addresses), `59` symbol census tables (`18,293` rows), and `15` modular binary patch sets (`753` addresses).

- Full single-file technical compendium for LLMs: [https://nfsu.cc/llms-full.txt](https://nfsu.cc/llms-full.txt)
- Atom RSS feed (engineering updates): [https://nfsu.cc/feed.xml](https://nfsu.cc/feed.xml)
- Source code & architecture: [https://github.com/Caliko06/need-for-speed-underground-browser](https://github.com/Caliko06/need-for-speed-underground-browser)

## Global Reverse Engineering & Static Recompilation Hub (ELI5 + Technical, EN)

- [Reverse Engineering & Static Recompilation Field Guide](https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/index.html) ([Markdown](https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/index.md)): ELI5 + Deep Dive playbooks for x86->C->WASM lifting, compiler passes, DirectX 9->WebGPU, V8 WASM caching, and evidence-first AI binary analysis.
- [Binary Symbol Census & V/I/U Naming Methodology](https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/symbols.html) ([Markdown](https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/symbols.md)): 59 tables, 18,293 symbol rows (7,886 V-verified).
- [Non-Destructive Modular Binary Patching](https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/patches.html) ([Markdown](https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/patches.md)): 15 topic modules covering 753 unique hex addresses.
